agents.description: Which agents may use the action: dimmi (answers customers), operator (works for the team), or both.

approval.description: Who on the team must approve a call before it runs: none, teammate or admin. Only a write action can need approval.

approval_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes a call waits for a teammate's approval before it expires, from 1 to 10080. Defaults to 60.

body_encoding.description: How the request body is sent: json or form.

body_template.description: The request body as JSON, with placeholders such as {input.order_id}, {contact.email} or {connection.region} filled in at call time. Null when the request has no body.

bound_arguments.description: Arguments of an MCP tool that the admin fills in and the model never sees, by argument name. Values may hold placeholders such as {contact.email}. Empty when none.

channels.description: Channels on which the action is offered, such as ["widget"]. Defaults to the widget alone.

confirmation.description: Whether the customer must confirm a call before it runs: none or customer. Only a write action can ask for it.

connection_id.description: Id of the connection the action sends its requests through, such as acn_... Send it wherever an action connection is asked for.

created_at.description: When it was created, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

description.description: What the action does, written for the model that decides when to call it. 10 to 1024 characters.

error_message_path.description: Dotted path into a failed response's body where the error message is found, such as error.message. Null when none is set.

has_unpublished_changes.description: True when this working copy differs from the published version, or nothing was published yet. The agent only runs the published version.

headers.description: Extra request headers by name. Values may hold placeholders such as {input.locale}. Empty when none.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema object of the arguments the model must give when it calls the action.

kind.description: How the action runs: http sends a request to an API, mcp_tool calls a tool on an MCP server.

last_test_response.description: The result of the last successful live test of the action, kept to help map response fields. Left out when there is none.

mcp_tool_name.description: Name of the tool called on the MCP server. Null for an http action.

method.description: HTTP method of the request: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Null for an mcp_tool action.

name.description: The tool name the model calls the action by: 3 to 48 lowercase letters, digits and underscores, such as lookup_order.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

path_template.description: Path added to the connection's base URL, with placeholders, such as /orders/{input.order_id}. Null for an mcp_tool action.

query.description: Query string parameters by name. Values may hold placeholders such as {input.status}. Empty when none.

response_fields.description: Which values of the response the model gets to read, each a name and a dotted path into the body. Empty when nothing is mapped.

response_max_bytes.description: Largest response body the action accepts, in bytes, from 1024 to 262144. Defaults to 65536.

side_effect.description: Whether a call only reads data (read) or changes something (write). A read runs at once; a write may wait for confirmation or approval.

source.description: How the action was made: dashboard, api or mcp_sync (created from an MCP server's tool list).

status.description: Where the action stands: draft (never published), published (the agent can use it) or disabled (switched off).

timeout_ms.description: How long a call may take, in milliseconds, from 1000 to 15000. Null uses the connection's timeout.

title.description: Short name people see for the action, up to 80 characters, such as Look up an order.

updated_at.description: When it last changed, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

warnings.description: Notes about the action's definition. Currently always an empty list.

agents.description: dimmi (answers customers) and operator (works for the team). Default dimmi only.

approval.description: none, teammate or admin: who on the team must approve a write before it runs.

approval_timeout_minutes.description: A length of time in minutes, such as 30.

body_encoding.description: How the request body is sent: "json" or "form". Left out, it is "json". With "form" the body_template must be a flat object of plain values, such as {"email": "{contact.email}"}.

body_template.description: JSON body sent with the request, only for POST, PUT and PATCH. Values may hold placeholders {input.x}, {contact.x} or {connection.x}, such as {"order_id": "{input.order_id}", "reason": "{input.reason}"}. Send null to clear the body.

bound_arguments.description: For an action on an MCP connection: arguments you fix yourself, hidden from the model and laid over what the model sends. An object of argument name to value; values may hold placeholders, such as {"account_id": "{connection.account_id}", "limit": 10}.

channels.description: Where dimmi may take it, such as widget. Default widget.

confirmation.description: none, or customer to have the customer confirm a write first (the default).

description.description: When to use the action, 10 to 1024 characters; the model reads it to decide.

error_message_path.description: Dotted path to the error message in the other system's JSON response, read when a call fails. Letters, digits, _ , - and # joined by dots, at most 200 characters, such as "error.message".

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers sent with the request, as an object of header name to value, at most 10, such as {"X-Api-Version": "2024-01"}. Not allowed: Host, Cookie, Content-Length, Content-Type, Transfer-Encoding, Authorization, Idempotency-Key, User-Agent, Connection and any name starting with Dimmi-.

method.description: HTTP method of an action on an http connection: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE (lowercase is accepted). Left out on create, it is GET. Not used for an action on an mcp connection. Such as "POST".

name.description: Tool name the model sees: 3 to 48 lowercase letters, digits and underscores.

query.description: Words to search for, such as refund.

response_fields.description: Which values of the response the model reads, at most 30; left empty, it reads the whole response. response_max_bytes.description: A size in bytes, such as 65536.

restore_version_id.description: Id of the saved version, starting with prcv or srsv_, such as prcv_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with the matching versions list.

side_effect.description: read runs at once; write changes something and may wait for agreement. Default write.

status.description: When creating: has no effect, a new action always starts as a draft and goes live through POST /ai/actions/{action}/publications, so leave it out. title.description: The title of the action.

error_code.description: Why the call failed, such as auth_failed, not_found, upstream_rejected, rate_limited, unavailable, host_blocked or response_too_large. Null when it did not fail.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

input.description: The arguments the model gave, frozen when the call was proposed. Left out unless the caller may read payloads.

latency_ms.description: How long the request took, in milliseconds. Null when nothing was sent.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

request.description: The request that was sent, as JSON. Left out unless the caller may read payloads.

requested_at.description: When the agent asked for the call.

response.description: What the workspace's API or MCP server answered, as JSON. Left out unless the caller may read payloads.

result.description: The shaped result the model read: only the mapped response fields, or an error and message. Left out unless the caller may read payloads.

title.description: The action's short name at the time of the call, such as Refund an order.

default_headers.description: Headers sent with every request of this connection, by name. Empty when none.

variables.description: Plain named values that request templates read as {connection.<name>}, such as a region or account id. Not for secrets. Empty when none.

kind.description: What relies on the agent: workflow, series, connection, room, inbox or agent.

name.description: Its name.

ties.description: What still relies on the agent: workflows and series that name it, places it answers on and agents that may transfer to it. The agent can be archived only once this is empty.

created_at.description: When it was created, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

data_type.description: What the value is: text, number, date, boolean or choice.

description.description: What the AI looks for. Empty when not set.

label.description: What the team calls the attribute.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

options.description: With choice, the values it may take. Empty otherwise.

status.description: active while the AI reads it, archived once it stopped.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

inbox_ids.description: Ids of the inboxes whose new conversations the agent takes, each starting with inbox_.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

created_at.description: When it was created, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

version.description: draft runs the working copy, live the published one. Left out, it is draft.

description.description: The text explaining what the topic covers, shown to people choosing their subscriptions. Empty when none was written.

name.description: The topic's name, such as Product updates.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

subscribed_count.description: How many people the topic reaches now.

unsubscribed_count.description: How many people have left this topic.

archived.description: true archives it, false brings it back; the choices people made are kept.

description.description: What people get under it, up to 300 characters.

name.description: Name people see, up to 80 characters and unlike the other topics.

description.description: The text explaining what the topic covers. Empty when none was written.

name.description: The topic's name, such as Product updates.

subscribed.description: True when this person currently receives broadcasts under the topic.

data.description: One result per conversation, in the order the ids were sent: whether it went through, the fields that changed, or the error code that stopped it.

conversation_ids.description: Ids of conversations, as a list, such as ["conv_01jx2m8k4t"].

trash.description: Set true to move every listed conversation to the trash instead of changing it. Send this or changes, never both. Example: true.

code.description: The machine-readable code of the error that stopped this member's change, such as not_found.

message.description: A sentence explaining why the change failed, in the caller's language when a translation exists.

data.description: One result per member id sent, in the order sent: its status and, when it failed, the error.

skipped.description: How many members were left alone because they already had the values asked for.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

status.description: What came of this member's change: updated, skipped (already had the values asked for) or failed (see error).

provider.description: The captcha service asked for on sign-up and when mailing sign-in links. Only turnstile is offered.

site_key.description: The public site key the browser uses to show the captcha challenge.

cached_input_per_mtok.description: Price in US dollars per million cached input tokens, as a decimal string. Null when the price list does not know this model.

context_tokens.description: The size of the model's context window, in tokens.

display_name.description: The model's name as shown to people in settings.

family.description: The model's family: anthropic, openai or openweight.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

input_per_mtok.description: Price in US dollars per million input tokens, as a decimal string. Null when the price list does not know this model.

output_per_mtok.description: Price in US dollars per million output tokens, as a decimal string. Null when the price list does not know this model.

suggested.description: The jobs this model is suggested for: any of answer, classifier and fallback.

daily.description: Views of the changelog's updates for each day of the period, as a date and a count.

days.description: How many days the report covers, counting today; between 1 and 90.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

reactions.description: How many reactions readers left on updates over the period.

since.description: The first day the report covers, as a date such as 2026-11-01.

subscribers.description: How many people subscribe to the changelog now.

subscribers_joined.description: How many people subscribed during the period.

subscribers_unsubscribed.description: How many people unsubscribed during the period.

top_entries.description: The most read updates of the period, each with its id, title, slug, publish time, views and reactions.

views.description: Total views of the changelog's updates over the period.

date.description: The day counted, as a date such as 2026-11-01.

views.description: How many times updates were viewed that day.

counts.description: How many entries are in each status, keyed by status (draft, scheduled, published), such as {"draft": 3, "published": 12}.

data.description: The entries on this page, without their bodies; read one entry to get body_markdown.

links.description: Optional URLs for moving through the list, such as the next page. Left out when there are none.

authors.description: The teammates shown as the entry's authors, each with member id, name and avatar. While nobody has chosen authors, these are the editors.

authors_chosen.description: True when someone picked the entry's authors by hand; false while the people who edited it stand as its authors.

body_markdown.description: The working copy of the entry's body, in Markdown. Present when one entry is read; left out of lists.

cover_url.description: URL of the entry's cover image. Null when it has none.

created_at.description: When it was created, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

editors.description: The teammates who edited the entry, each with member id, name and avatar.

has_unpublished_changes.description: True when a published entry's working copy differs from what readers see, so it needs publishing again. Always false for drafts and scheduled entries.

help_center_id.description: Id of the help center whose changelog holds this entry, starting with hc_. Send it wherever a help center is asked for.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

labels.description: The labels the entry is filed under, each with id, name, slug and color.

lock_version.description: A number that goes up with every save, starting at 1. Send the value you read back when updating so a newer edit is not overwritten.

notified_at.description: When subscribers were mailed about this entry; an entry mails only once. Null when no mailing has gone out.

notify_subscribers.description: True when subscribers are to be mailed when the entry is published.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

published_at.description: When the entry was published. Null while it has never been published.

scheduled_for.description: When a scheduled entry will publish itself. Null when no publish time is set.

slug.description: The entry's URL name within the changelog, such as dark-mode-is-here.

status.description: Where the entry stands: draft, scheduled or published.

summary.description: A short summary of the entry. Null when none was written.

title.description: The entry's title.

email.description: The email address updates are sent to.

custom_attributes.description: The company's custom attributes as an object of names and values, such as {"plan": "pro"}. An empty object when it has none.

domain.description: The company's web domain, such as acme.com, used to match it when it has no external id. Null when unknown.

external_id.description: The company's id in your own system, unique within the workspace. Null when none was given.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

name.description: The company's name.

notes.description: Free-text notes the team keeps about the company. Null when there are none.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

people_count.description: How many contacts belong to the company. Given only in lists; absent when one company is read.

tags.description: The tags on the company, each with its id and name.

updated_at.description: When it last changed, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

custom_attributes.description: The company's custom attribute values, as an object of attribute key to value, with keys as GET /attribute-definitions defines them for companies. When the company already exists they are merged over the ones it has. Such as {"plan": "enterprise"}.

domain.description: The company's domain name, at most 255 characters, such as acme.com. When a company is looked up (a contact's company, or an upsert), it is found by external_id first, then by this; a contact's company needs one of the two.

external_id.description: Your own system's id of the company, 1 to 255 characters, such as org_512. When a company is looked up (a contact's company, or an upsert), it is found by this first, then by domain; a new one is added when none matches.

name.description: The company's name, 1 to 255 characters, such as Acme Inc.

name.description: The company's name.

client_id.description: OpenID Connect only: the client id dimmi signs in with at the identity provider. Absent on SAML connections.

idp_certificates.description: SAML only: the identity provider's signing certificates, PEM encoded. Absent on OpenID Connect connections.

idp_entity_id.description: SAML only: the identity provider's entity id. Absent on OpenID Connect connections.

idp_metadata_url.description: SAML only: the URL of the identity provider's metadata, which its settings are refreshed from. Absent when none was given.

idp_sso_url.description: SAML only: the identity provider's sign-in URL people are sent to. Absent on OpenID Connect connections.

issuer.description: OpenID Connect only: the identity provider's issuer URL. Absent on SAML connections.

name_id_format.description: SAML only: the NameID format asked of the identity provider. Absent when none is set.

scopes.description: OpenID Connect only: the scopes asked for at sign-in. Absent when none are set.

sp_certificate.description: SAML only: dimmi's own service provider certificate, made with the connection, to give to the identity provider.

button_color.description: The color of buttons as #RRGGBB, such as #1f2328. Falls back to primary_color when no button color is set.

button_ink.description: The text color that reads on button_color: dark on a light color, light on a dark one.

font.description: The messenger's font: system for the device's font or inherit to take the host page's.

header_color.description: The color of the header as #RRGGBB. Falls back to primary_color when no header color is set.

header_ink.description: The text color that reads on header_color: dark on a light color, light on a dark one.

padding_x.description: How far the launcher sits from the side edge of the page, in pixels, 0 to 200. Defaults to 20.

padding_y.description: How far the launcher sits from the bottom edge of the page, in pixels, 0 to 200. Defaults to 20.

position.description: The side of the page the launcher sits on: right or left.

primary_color.description: The messenger's brand color as #RRGGBB, such as #1f2328.

sound.description: True when the messenger plays a sound for new messages.

theme.description: The messenger's color theme: light, dark or auto to follow the visitor's device.

fade.description: True when the background softens into the page below it.

image_url.description: URL of the background image. Absent when there is none.

type.description: What fills the home hero and header: solid, gradient or image.

logo_url.description: URL of the workspace's logo. Null when it has none.

name.description: The workspace's name, which the messenger speaks for.

console.description: True when the messenger captures the browser's console output for the team.

network.description: True when the messenger captures the browser's network activity for the team.

ai_agent.description: True when the AI agent is available in the messenger.

allow_anonymous.description: True when visitors who are not signed in may use the messenger. Always false when identity_mode is required.

attachments.description: True when visitors may attach files to messages.

collect_email.description: When the messenger asks a visitor for their email: never, offline (only when the team is away) or always.

help_tab.description: True when the help tab is on and the messenger has a help center to show.

identity_mode.description: Whether the host app must sign visitors in: off, optional or required.

intercom_shim.description: True when the messenger also answers Intercom's JavaScript calls, for sites moving from Intercom.

max_attachment_mb.description: The largest file a visitor may attach, in megabytes.

opener.description: True when a workflow greets visitors as they open a chat, instead of the conversation starting from their first message.

require_email_when_offline.description: True when a visitor must give an email to write while the team is away.

icon.description: The icon shown beside the link: link, calendar, book, mail, phone, chat, video or help.

title.description: The link's text on the messenger's home screen.

url.description: The address the link opens.

icon.description: The icon on the launcher: chat, help or wave.

image_url.description: URL of a custom launcher image. Null when the launcher uses its icon.

label.description: The text on the launcher, up to 24 characters. Empty when it shows none.

shape.description: The launcher's shape: circle or squircle.

style.description: How the launcher shows: bubble, tab or hidden.

enabled.description: True when a privacy notice shows above the composer.

url.description: The address of the privacy policy the notice links to. Null when none is set.

polling_interval_ms.description: How often, in milliseconds, a browser should poll for updates when it cannot hold a live stream.

token_url.description: The address the browser asks for a token to open the live stream.

url.description: The address of the live update stream.

dynamic.description: True when the messenger's rules depend on page conditions the browser must check.

version.description: The messenger's config version these rules were read at; it goes up when the messenger's settings change.

confirmed_until.description: Until when sensitive steps need no new proof of who the caller is, as a UTC time. After it, confirm again.

method.description: How the caller last proved who they are: password, or email_code for an account without a password.

workspace_name.description: The name of the workspace the app was given access to. Empty when the access names no workspace.

header_name.description: Needed when auth_type is api_key_header: the name of the HTTP header the key travels in. 1 to 64 letters, digits or hyphens, such as X-Api-Key.

prefix.description: Only for auth_type bearer: the word put before the token in the Authorization header in place of Bearer, such as Token. Left out, it is Bearer.

blocked.description: True when the team has blocked this contact.

email_verified.description: True only when a trusted source proved the email belongs to this contact; an address a lead typed stays false.

external_id.description: The contact's id in your own system. Null when none was given.

metadata_url.description: SAML only: address of dimmi's metadata for this connection, which the identity provider can read its settings from.

redirect_uri.description: OpenID Connect only: dimmi's address sign-ins come back to. Register it with the identity provider.

app_version.description: Version of the user's own app the session belongs to; null for a browser.

auth_method.description: How the session signed in, such as password, magic_link, email_code, passkey, sso or google.

auth_methods.description: Every method used to sign the session in, such as password and totp; empty when none is recorded.

authenticated_at.description: When the user last proved who they are on this session.

client.description: Name of the user's own app the session belongs to; null for a browser.

country.description: Country the session was last used from; null when unknown.

created_at.description: When it was created, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

current.description: True for the session making this request.

device_label.description: Readable name of the device or browser, such as Chrome on macOS; null when unknown.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

ip.description: IP address the session was last used from; null when unknown.

kind.description: Kind of session, such as browser.

last_activity_at.description: When the session was last used.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

platform.description: Platform of the user's own app the session belongs to; null for a browser.

two_factor_used.description: True when a second factor was used to sign the session in.

card_numbers.description: True when payment card numbers are redacted from messages; on by default.

us_ssn.description: True when US social security numbers are redacted from messages; off by default.

brand_color.description: Color used in branded replies, as # and six hex digits, such as #10b981. Only used when template is branded.

bulk_mail_handling.description: What happens to bulk mail such as newsletters that starts a new thread: close files it as a closed conversation, open leaves it open, drop ignores it. New addresses use close.

footer_markdown.description: Footer that closes branded replies, written in Markdown, at most 500 characters, such as Sent by the Acme support team.

quote_previous.description: true puts the message being answered below each reply; false leaves it out. New addresses start with true.

template.description: Look of replies from this address: plain or branded. Branded uses brand_color and footer_markdown.

options.description: For a passkey: the options the browser's credential API creates the passkey with. Left out for other factors.

otpauth_url.description: For an authenticator app: the otpauth:// address that adds the account to the app. Left out for other factors.

qr_svg.description: For an authenticator app: the otpauth address drawn as a QR code, as SVG markup. Left out for other factors.

secret.description: For an authenticator app: the secret to type into the app by hand. Shown once; left out for other factors.

deep_link.description: Link to the right settings screen in the mail service; null when there is none.

key.description: Name of the mail service the guide is for, such as gmail, google_workspace or microsoft_365.

name.description: Name of the mail service as people read it, such as Google Workspace.

provider.description: Same value as key, kept for older readers. Use key.

recommended.description: True for the guide that fits the address's domain; it is listed first.

steps.description: The steps to set forwarding up, in order, with this address's own addresses filled in.

warnings.description: What tends to go wrong in this mail service; empty for none.

equals.description: Values of the other field under which this one shows. Left out when any value is enough.

field.description: Key of the other ticket field that must have a value for this one to show.

equals.description: The values of the other field that make this field show, as a list of up to 50 texts, such as ["refund", "exchange"]. Left out or empty, this field shows whenever the other field has any value.

field.description: Key of another field of the same ticket type that this field depends on: it must have a value for this field to show. At most 40 characters, such as reason.

sessions_revoked.description: How many of the contact's messenger sessions were ended.

note.description: Note the agent left for the team at the handover. Left out when there is none.

priority.description: Priority the handover set on the conversation. Left out when it set none.

reason.description: Why the simulated turn handed over, such as customer_requested, unknown, frustration, safety or max_replies.

team_id.description: Id of the team the handover sent the conversation to, such as team_.... Left out when it chose none.

role.description: Who wrote this earlier message: customer or agent, such as "customer".

text.description: What that earlier message said, at most 4000 characters, such as Hi, where is my order?

action_id.description: Id of the action whose write is waiting, such as aac_....

args.description: The arguments the action was called with, as an object.

state.description: What the write waits on: awaiting_confirmation for the customer's yes, pending_approval for a teammate's approval.

summary.description: One line saying what the write would do.

tool.description: Name of the tool the agent called for the action.

action_id.description: Id of the action whose write is waiting, starting with aac_, such as aac_01jx2m8k4t, copied from the last turn's state. Put it in confirmed_action_ids to confirm it.

args.description: The arguments the waiting write would be called with, as an object, copied unchanged from the last turn's state, such as {"order_id": "1042"}.

state.description: Why the write waits, copied from the last turn's state: awaiting_confirmation (the customer must confirm) or pending_approval (a teammate must approve).

summary.description: The short text that says what the waiting write would do, copied unchanged from the last turn's state.

tool.description: The tool name of the action whose write is waiting, copied unchanged from the last turn's state.

attributes.description: The made-up customer's custom attributes, as an object of attribute key to value. They count as trusted. Such as {"plan": "pro"}.

channel.description: The channel the made-up customer writes from: widget, email, slack, whatsapp, instagram, facebook or api. Left out or empty, it is widget. Such as "email".

company.description: The custom attributes of the made-up customer's company, as an object of attribute key to value, such as {"plan": "enterprise"}.

email.description: The made-up customer's email address, at most 320 characters, such as ada@example.com.

external_id.description: Your own system's id of the made-up customer, at most 200 characters, such as user_8421. Giving one makes them a known user, not a lead.

inbox_id.description: Id of the inbox the made-up conversation is placed in, starting with inbox_, such as inbox_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /inboxes.

name.description: The made-up customer's name, at most 200 characters, such as Ada Lovelace.

verified.description: true when the made-up customer is signed in, so their identity and email count as verified; false or left out for an unverified visitor.

branches.description: Branches of the procedure taken so far in the simulated conversation, as an object of strings. Send the whole state back with the next turn.

called_action_ids.description: Ids of the actions called so far in the simulated conversation. Send the whole state back with the next turn.

completed_step_ids.description: Ids of the procedure steps completed so far. Send the whole state back with the next turn.

pending.description: Writes that wait on the customer's confirmation or a teammate's approval; empty for none.

procedure_id.description: Id of the procedure the simulated conversation is running, such as prc_.... Left out when it runs none.

status.description: Where the procedure stands: active, completed, handed_off or exited. Left out when no procedure runs.

step_outputs.description: What the procedure's steps produced so far, as an object. Send the whole state back with the next turn.

branches.description: Copy it unchanged from the state the last preview turn handed back: an object of step id to the side that step took.

called_action_ids.description: Copy it unchanged from the state the last preview turn handed back: the list of ids of the actions already called, such as ["aac_01jx2m8k4t"].

completed_step_ids.description: Copy it unchanged from the state the last preview turn handed back: the list of ids of the procedure's steps already done.

pending.description: Copy it unchanged from the state the last preview turn handed back: the list of writes still waiting to be confirmed or approved, each with action_id, tool, args, state and summary.

procedure_id.description: Id of the procedure the conversation is in, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t, copied from the state the last preview turn handed back.

status.description: Where the procedure stands, copied from the state the last preview turn handed back: active, completed, handed_off or exited. Only active carries the procedure on.

step_outputs.description: Copy it unchanged from the state the last preview turn handed back: an object of what the procedure's steps have produced so far.

agent_id.description: Id of the agent the conversation was passed to (starts with aia_).

from_name.description: Name of the agent that passed the conversation on.

name.description: Name of the agent the conversation was passed to.

summary.description: What the first agent told the next one about the conversation so far.

action_mocks.description: What each action answers instead of really being called, as an object keyed by action id; each value has status (HTTP status, 100 to 599) and body (any JSON), such as {"aac_abc123": {"status": 200, "body": {"order": {"status": "shipped"}}}}. An action with no mock answers with the result of its last live test.

confirmed_action_ids.description: Ids of the waiting writes you confirm or approve this turn, taken from action_id in the pending list of the state the last simulated turn handed back (send that state as active_state). At most 10, such as ["aac_abc123"]. You may send these without a message.

history.description: The turns so far, oldest first, as returned by earlier calls.

message.description: What the customer writes, up to 4000 characters.

source_conversation_id.description: Id of the conversation, such as conv_01jx2m8k4t, or its number, such as 1042 for #1042. Find it with GET /conversations or GET /search.

stream_id.description: An id you make up, at most 64 characters, so the run reports its progress live on your own realtime channel while it happens. Only useful to a client listening on that channel; leave it out otherwise. Such as "sim-7f3a2c".

target.description: draft tests the working copy, live the published one.

attributes.description: The made-up person's attributes, by key.

email.description: The made-up person's email address.

name.description: The made-up person's name.

reason.description: Why the tool could not be turned into an action.

tool.description: Name of the MCP server's tool that the sync skipped.

created_at.description: When it was created, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

external_id.description: Slack's id of the workspace (team) the app is installed in; null until it is connected.

external_name.description: Name of the Slack workspace the app is installed in; empty until it is known.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

inbound_transport.description: How Slack delivers events to dimmi: webhook or socket. Empty until it is known.

last_error.description: Why the connection last failed; null when it is healthy.

mode.description: How the connection was made: custom for the workspace's own Slack app, shared for the install's shared app. Empty until it is known.

name.description: The connection's name in dimmi.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

status.description: Where the connection stands: pending, active, error or disconnected.

type.description: Kind of channel; slack for a Slack connection.

updated_at.description: When it last changed, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

id.description: The id of this record. Send it wherever an endpoint asks for this record; never use its name or title in its place.

is_private.description: True for a private Slack channel.

name.description: The Slack channel's name.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

channel_id.description: Id of the Slack connection that watches the channel, such as chn_....

external_id.description: Slack's own id of the channel, such as C0123ABCD.

is_shared_external.description: True when the Slack channel is shared with another organization.

last_error.description: Why watching the channel last failed; null when it is healthy.

last_seen_event_at.description: When an event from the channel last arrived; null if none has.

mode.description: Who counts as the customer in the channel: shared (the other organization's people), community (everyone but linked teammates), helpdesk (the team's colleagues) or internal (nobody).

name.description: The Slack channel's name.

object.description: The kind of record this is, the same for every record of its kind, such as article.

removed_at.description: When the app was removed from the channel; null while it is still in it. A removed room keeps its settings.

settings.description: The settings an admin chose for the channel, as an object; empty for none.

status.description: Whether the channel is watched: active, paused, removed or error.

trigger.description: When a message in the channel becomes a conversation: author_window, every_message, emoji, mention, ai, auto or off.

updated_at.description: When it last changed, as an RFC 3339 time, such as 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.

agent_delay_seconds.description: Seconds the AI agent waits before answering in this room so a teammate can reply first, from 0 to 900, such as 120.

agent_delay_when.description: When the agent's wait applies: always, or inside_hours to wait only during office hours.

agent_mode.description: How the AI agent works in this room: auto lets it answer, draft makes it write drafts instead.

auto_join.description: true or false: the auto-join flag stored on this room.

auto_reply_after_seconds.description: Seconds after a new conversation starts before the automatic reply is posted, from 0 to 900; 0 sends no automatic reply. Such as 60.

request_sensitivity.description: How readily a message counts as a request: conservative needs more confidence, aggressive accepts less.

triage_channel_id.description: Slack's own id of the channel where this room's new conversations are posted for triage, 1 to 40 characters, such as C0123ABCD.

complete.description: True once the connection is active, so its Slack app needs no more setting up.

create_app_url.description: Address that opens Slack's app creation with the manifest filled in.

interactions_url.description: dimmi's address Slack sends button clicks and other interactions to.

manifest.description: The Slack app manifest that sets the app up, as an object to paste into Slack.

request_url.description: dimmi's address Slack delivers events to.

option.description: The key of one of this conversation's snooze choices, from GET /snooze-options, at most 40 characters. With then=snooze send exactly one of until, preset or option.

preset.description: When the snooze ends, as a preset: later_today, tomorrow, next_week or one_week, such as "tomorrow". With then=snooze send exactly one of until, preset or option.

until.description: When the snooze ends, as an ISO 8601 time, such as 2026-12-01T09:00:00Z. With then=snooze send exactly one of until, preset or option.

weekday.description: Weekday the snooze ends on, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday, for the kind weekday_at. Left out otherwise.

new_article_title.description: Only to rename the article: its new title, such as Returns and refunds.

reason.description: Why, in one or two short, plain sentences a teammate reads at a glance: what is wrong today and what this changes. No tool names or ids.

reason.description: Why, in one or two short, plain sentences a teammate reads at a glance: what is wrong today and what this changes. No tool names or ids.

bot_token.description: The app's bot token, starting with xoxb-.

signing_secret.description: The app's signing secret, needed with webhook.

include_notes.description: true to add the team's internal notes, which stay out by default.

assignee_id.description: mem_..., me, or null for nobody. A teammate's conversation is theirs by default.

author.description: member (default): you write first and the customer receives it. contact: you record what the customer wrote.

author_id.description: Import only, author member: the teammate (mem_...) who wrote the first message.

body.description: The first message in Markdown. As a teammate, the customer receives exactly this text.

closed_at.description: Import only, with status closed: when it closed; the first message's time by default.

external_id.description: Import only: the conversation's id in the tool it comes from; sending it again returns the first copy.

inbox_id.description: With author contact: the inbox (inbox_...) whose API channel takes the message.

status.description: Import only: open (default) or closed.

subject.description: The subject of the conversation, at most 255 characters.

message_id.description: Optional message (msg_...) that prompted the tags.

tags.description: Tag ids (tag_...) or names, up to 50. Names match whatever their case.

definition.description: The conditions as JSON: {"op":"and","groups":[{"op":"or","conditions":[{"field":"priority","op":"in","value":["high","urgent"]}]}]}, op and or or, up to 5 groups and 20 conditions. Fields: status, channel, channel_connection, inbox, contact, assignee (me works), team, tag, company, priority, unread, waiting, imported, number, message_count, subject, created_at, last_message_at, waiting_since, snoozed_until, closed_at. Ops: in and not_in with a list of values or ids, exists and not_exists, eq for true or false, eq, gt and lt for numbers, eq, gte and lte for priority, contains for subject, before and after with an RFC 3339 time, older_than and newer_than with a duration such as P3D or PT2H.

icon.description: An icon as one emoji, such as 📦.

name.description: Up to 60 characters.

attachment_ids.description: Up to 10 ids (att_...) of files already uploaded.

lock_version.description: The lock_version the article had when you read it. Send it with every save.

client_writable.description: Contacts only: true lets the messenger set it from the browser, so its values are claimed, not trusted. 20 attributes at most.

description.description: The description of the attribute definition, at most 500 characters.

label.description: The new name people see for the attribute, 1 to 80 characters. Such as Plan tier.

options.description: The values a list attribute may take: 1 to 200 different non-empty strings, replacing the old list. Only for attributes whose data type is list; other types refuse any options. Such as ["free","pro","enterprise"].

status.description: active or archived.

code.description: The first code from the authenticator app, which activates a pending factor, such as 123456.

credential.description: The JSON object the device signed, which activates a pending passkey, sent instead of a code. At most 16 KB.

name.description: A new name for the factor, up to 60 characters, such as Work phone. It cannot be empty.

preferred.description: true to make this the factor asked for first at sign-in. Recovery codes cannot be preferred.

author_ids.description: Ids of teammates (mem_...), at most 5; an empty list shows the editors again.

body_markdown.description: The full new entry in Markdown; it replaces the old text entirely.

cover_url.description: An image address from this help center, such as one already used in an article.

label_ids.description: Ids of changelog labels, as a list, such as ["cll_01jx2m8k4t"]. Find them with GET /help-centers/{help_center}/changelog-labels.

lock_version.description: The lock_version the entry had when you read it. Send it with every save.

slug.description: The part of the address that names it, in lowercase words joined by hyphens, such as refund-policy.

summary.description: One or two sentences that sum it up.

title.description: The title of the changelog entry, at most 150 characters.

add_tags.description: Tag ids or names to add; a new name becomes a tag. 50 at most.

custom_attributes.description: Values by key, merged into what the company has. null removes a key.

name.description: The name of the company.

notes.description: Team-only notes, 10,000 characters at most, replacing the current notes.

body.description: The text of the contact note, at most 10000 characters.

pinned.description: true to pin it to the top, false to unpin it.

add_tags.description: Tag ids or names to add; a new name becomes a tag. 50 at most.

blocked.description: true blocks the contact, which also hides them from the list; false unblocks.

company_id.description: Id of the company (cmp_...) to link, or null to unlink.

custom_attributes.description: Values by key, merged into what the contact has. null removes a key.

email.description: An email address, such as ana@example.com.

external_id.description: Your own system's id of this record, such as user_8421.

name.description: The name of the contact.

notes.description: Team-only notes, 10,000 characters at most, replacing the current notes.

phone.description: A phone number with its country code, such as +14155550123.

delay_minutes.description: 0 asks straight away, 10 after ten minutes, 60 after an hour.

email.description: true asks email conversations' customers by email.

enabled.description: true asks customers to rate conversations when they close.

include_agent_closed.description: true also asks when the AI agent closed the conversation.

add_tags.description: Tags to put on the conversation, or on each one in a bulk change, as a list of up to 50 tag ids (tag_...) or tag names; a name no tag has yet becomes a new tag. Such as ["tag_01jx2m8k4t", "billing"].

ai_enabled.description: false keeps every AI agent off the conversation, or each one in a bulk change, until turned on again; true lets the agent answer again, even after a handover.

assignee_id.description: Who the conversation, or each one in a bulk change, goes to: a teammate's id starting with mem_, such as mem_01jx2m8k4t (find it with GET /members), me for yourself, or null to hand it to nobody.

inbox_id.description: Id of the inbox to move the conversation, or each one in a bulk change, to, starting with inbox_, such as inbox_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /inboxes.

note.description: Only with status closed: a note for the team kept with the closing, 1 to 65536 characters, such as Refund sent, nothing more to do.

priority.description: How urgent the conversation is, or each one in a bulk change: none, low, medium, high or urgent, such as "high".

remove_tags.description: Tags to take off the conversation, or off each one in a bulk change, as a list of up to 50 tag ids (tag_...), such as ["tag_01jx2m8k4t"]. Find them with GET /tags.

snooze_option.description: Only with status snoozed: the key of one of the workspace's own snooze choices, from GET /snooze-options, at most 40 characters. Send exactly one of snoozed_until, snooze_preset or snooze_option.

snooze_preset.description: Only with status snoozed: later_today (three hours on), tomorrow or next_week (at nine) or one_week (seven days on, at nine), in your time zone, such as "tomorrow". Send exactly one of snoozed_until, snooze_preset or snooze_option.

snoozed_until.description: Only with status snoozed: when the snooze ends, as an RFC 3339 (ISO 8601) time from a minute to a year ahead, such as 2026-12-01T09:00:00Z. Send exactly one of snoozed_until, snooze_preset or snooze_option.

spam.description: true moves the conversation, or each one in a bulk change, to the spam view and out of every other; false brings it back.

status.description: The status to set: open, closed or snoozed, such as "closed". snoozed also needs exactly one of snoozed_until, snooze_preset or snooze_option. A closed conversation cannot be snoozed: reopen it first.

subject.description: The new subject of the conversation, or of every conversation in a bulk change, 1 to 255 characters, such as Refund for order 1042.

team_id.description: Id of the team the conversation, or each one in a bulk change, goes to, starting with team_, such as team_01jx2m8k4t (find it with GET /teams), or null for no team.

unread.description: true marks the conversation, or each one in a bulk change, unread for you alone; false marks it read.

definition.description: The conditions as JSON: {"op":"and","groups":[{"op":"or","conditions":[{"field":"priority","op":"in","value":["high","urgent"]}]}]}, op and or or, up to 5 groups and 20 conditions. Fields: status, channel, channel_connection, inbox, contact, assignee (me works), team, tag, company, priority, unread, waiting, imported, number, message_count, subject, created_at, last_message_at, waiting_since, snoozed_until, closed_at. Ops: in and not_in with a list of values or ids, exists and not_exists, eq for true or false, eq, gt and lt for numbers, eq, gte and lte for priority, contains for subject, before and after with an RFC 3339 time, older_than and newer_than with a duration such as P3D or PT2H.

icon.description: An icon as one emoji, such as 📦.

name.description: The name of the conversation view, at most 60 characters.

sort.description: Order of the items. A leading minus, such as -created_at, puts the newest or largest first.

status_filter.description: open, snoozed, closed or any, or empty to clear.

customer_facing_name.description: The name customers see instead of the workspace's name. null removes it.

gif_picker.description: Whether teammates may search GIFs from the reply composer. On unless turned off; the picker also needs the install to have a GIF search key. Example: false.

locale.description: The fallback language for members and customers, such as en or de.

name.description: The name of the workspace, at most 80 characters.

require_two_factor.description: Cannot be changed through a token: the person must switch it in the app, after confirming their password.

seen_receipt_shows_name.description: Whether the customer's messenger names the teammate who read their message. Off by default: the customer only learns that the team saw it. Example: true.

seen_receipts.description: Whether the customer's messenger is told when the team read their message. On unless turned off. Example: false.

show_viewers_on_list.description: Whether the inbox list shows which teammates are viewing each conversation. On unless turned off. Example: false.

slug.description: The workspace's address: 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

team_mentions_enabled.description: Whether an internal note may mention a whole team. On unless turned off. Example: false.

test_mode.description: Fixed when the workspace is created; sending a different value is refused.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone, such as Europe/Berlin.

undo_send_seconds.description: How long a reply can be taken back after sending: 0, 5, 10, 20 or 30.

sso_connection_id.description: The id of the connection the domain's sign-ins go to, such as ssoc_4f9k2, or null for none. Required.

display_name.description: The name people see, such as Acme Support.

from_name_style.description: member_and_name names the teammate and the team; name_only names just the team.

inbox_id.description: Id of the inbox (inbox_...) new conversations land in.

is_default.description: true makes this the workspace's default address. The default cannot be turned off, only moved to another address.

reply_to_mode.description: token (default) adds a Reply-To address that threads answers back into their conversation; none leaves it out.

token.description: The secret from the confirmation link, sent in the body. Required; five wrong ones burn the link.

dns_host.description: The DNS host the person uses; an empty string goes back to the detected one.

mail_from_subdomain.description: The return path label, such as bounce.

body.description: Markdown, at most 2000 characters, with the placeholders {{member_name}}, {{member_title}}, {{address_name}} and {{company_name}}.

enabled.description: true to turn it on, false to turn it off.

claim.description: true when the person holding the link did not create the account and takes it over as they verify. false when left out.

token.description: The secret from the verification link, sent in the body. Required; five wrong ones burn the link.

client_writable.description: Whether the messenger may send this event from the visitor's browser. true opens the event name to the messenger, false closes it. Example: true.

description.description: The description of the event definition, at most 500 characters.

label.description: The new name people see for the event, 1 to 80 characters. Such as Checkout started.

status.description: active or archived.

messenger_new_events.description: Whether the messenger may send any event name, defining the ones the workspace has not seen before. A plain boolean; leaving it out counts as false. Example: true.

board_id.description: Id of another board (fbd_...) of the same help center to move it to.

body_markdown.description: The new description of the feedback request, written in Markdown, up to 65536 characters. Such as Customers want to **export** reports as CSV.

changelog_entry_id.description: With status: id of the changelog entry (cle_...) that shipped it, linked in the email once published.

merge_into_id.description: Id of the request (fbp_...) to keep. Votes and comments move there.

message.description: With status and notify: the team's note in the email, at most 2000 characters. Write it for customers.

moderation.description: approved shows a waiting request publicly; spam hides it.

notify.description: With status: true emails the voters and author that it moved. Ask the person first.

status.description: A status key from GET /feedback-statuses. Closed statuses leave the public roadmap.

title.description: The title of the feedback post, at most 150 characters.

ask_ai_enabled.description: Whether readers of the help center may ask a question and get an answer from its articles (the Ask AI feature). Example: true.

indexing_enabled.description: Whether search engines such as Google may index the help center's articles. false marks the site as not to be indexed. Example: true.

locale.description: A language code, such as en or pt-BR.

name.description: The name of the help center, at most 80 characters.

status.description: active serves the help center to readers; disabled takes it offline.

subdomain.description: 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and dashes, unique across the install. Changing it moves the public address.

name.description: The name of the identity secret, at most 60 characters.

reason.description: With status revoked: manual (default) or compromised.

retires_at.description: RFC 3339 time in the next 30 days, with status retiring; defaults to a week out.

revoke_sessions.description: With status revoked: false keeps the visitors it signed in; defaults to true.

status.description: retiring keeps it working until retires_at; revoked stops it now. A revoked secret cannot change again.

client_writable_attributes.description: The attribute keys a signed-in messenger may write itself: at most 20 distinct snake_case keys, such as ["plan", "company_size"]. The list replaces the stored one.

force.description: true to switch to required even when the counts fall short (100 session starts in the last week, 95% signed in). false when left out.

mode.description: off to ignore identity tokens, optional (the default) to prove signed-in customers and let others chat anonymously, or required so only proven customers get a messenger.

member_ids.description: With restricted: the teammates (mem_...) that may open it.

mode.description: everyone or restricted.

team_ids.description: With restricted: the teams (team_...) that may open it.

pinned_attributes.description: Customer attribute keys to pin beside conversations, up to 50.

sidebar.description: Free-form object of the caller's own inbox sidebar settings. It replaces the whole stored object, so send every key to keep. The dimmi app keeps keys such as pinned_views, hide_events and customer_time in it. Such as {"hide_events":true}.

views.description: Per view: sort, status, layout and columns, each a value a list accepts.

default_team_id.description: The team (team_...) new conversations go to, or null for none.

name.description: The name of the inbox, at most 80 characters.

settings.description: A merge patch: keys sent replace theirs, null resets a key to its default. reopen_window_days: how long after closing a customer's message reopens it, 0 for never. assign_on_reply: a reply takes a conversation nobody holds. color. assignment: {mode: manual, round_robin or balanced; include_away; overflow_team_id; queue_order: oldest_waiting or priority_then_oldest; default_capacity; capacity_by_channel}.

ticket_type_id.description: Id of the ticket type, starting with tktt_, such as tktt_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /ticket-types.

deploy_environment.description: The GitHub environment whose successful deployments count as a fix shipped, by name from the "environments" list of the repository, such as "production". Empty means any environment of the deploy repository.

deploy_repository.description: The GitHub repository whose successful deployments mark done issues as shipped, as owner/name from the tool's "teams" list, such as "acme/api". Empty turns this off.

from_email.description: An email address, such as support@example.com.

impact_field_id.description: Id of the ticket field, starting with tktf_, such as tktf_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /ticket-types/{type}/fields.

project_id.description: The default for new issues when none is picked: an id from the tool's "projects" list for the team, a Linear project or a Jira issue type, such as "10001". Empty clears it.

service_id.description: The default service new incidents are raised on when none is picked: an id from the tool's "services" list, such as "PABC123". Empty clears it.

severity_id.description: The default severity new incidents are declared with when none is picked: an id from the tool's "severities" list. Empty clears it.

signing_secret.description: The signing secret, as text. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.

states.description: A JSON object mapping the tool's status ids, from its "states" list, to the dimmi ticket state a ticket moves to, such as {"started": "tkts_01hzy3v8k2m4n6p8q0r2s4t6v8"}. It replaces the whole mapping; an empty value drops that status.

team_id.description: Id of the team, starting with team_, such as team_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /teams.

dims.description: Vector size the model returns, 64 to 4096.

embedding_key_id.description: Provider key (aik_...) to embed with; null or left out for the built-in embedder. Find it with GET /ai/keys.

model.description: Embedding model id on that key.

access_team_ids.description: Ids of the teams the conversation_access setting refers to, as a list, each starting with team_, such as ["team_01jx2m8k4t"]. Find them with GET /teams.

assign_on_reply.description: The member's own rule for taking a conversation by replying to it: inherit follows the inbox's rule, always assigns what they answer to them, never means replying does not assign it to them. When updating yourself it sets your own rule. Such as always.

away_reassign.description: Whether, while the member is away, conversations whose customers reply go back to the team. true is only accepted when the member is away; going online turns it off. When updating yourself it applies to your own conversations. Example: true.

capacity_by_channel.description: Object of the most open conversations the member holds per channel type: keys are widget, email or api, values are whole numbers from 1 to 500. It replaces the whole stored object. Such as {"email":20,"widget":5}.

conversation_access.description: Which conversations the member sees: all, assigned (only theirs), teams (their access teams) or all_except_teams. Owners always see everything. Nobody can change their own access, so it is refused when updating yourself. Such as all.

conversation_access_unassigned.description: Whether a narrow access mode also shows the member conversations nobody is assigned to. It is part of conversation access, which nobody can change for themselves, so it is refused when updating yourself. Example: true.

conversation_capacity.description: Most open conversations the member (or you, when updating yourself) holds at once, 1 to 500, such as 20. null for no limit.

custom_role_id.description: Id of a custom role to give the member, starting with rol_, such as rol_01jx2m8k4t, or null to take it away. Find it with GET /roles.

keep_owner.description: Only allowed together with role set to owner. true keeps you an owner too after making someone else an owner; otherwise you become an admin. Example: true.

reassign_to_member_id.description: With status deactivated: id of the teammate who takes the member's conversations, starting with mem_, such as mem_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /members. It has no use when updating yourself, since nobody deactivates themselves.

role.description: The member's built-in role: owner, admin or member. Any change to or from owner, your own included, needs an owner acting from their own browser in the app with a recent confirmation. Such as member.

status.description: Whether the member is active or deactivated. Nobody deactivates themselves, so deactivated is refused when updating yourself. Such as active.

all_inboxes.description: true goes back to every inbox.

digest_time.description: When digests post, as HH:MM in the workspace's time zone.

enabled.description: false turns it off; true turns it back on.

inbox_ids.description: Only conversations of these inboxes (inbox_...); left out means every inbox.

include_ai_handled.description: true also posts conversations the AI agent is handling.

name.description: A name for the team, up to 80 characters.

triggers.description: What it hears about: new_conversation, customer_replied, conversation_assigned, ai_handoff_requested and snooze_expired.

preferences.description: Up to 50 of {trigger, channel, enabled}. Triggers: new_conversation, conversation_assigned, customer_replied, mentioned, ai_handoff_requested, ai_action_approval_requested, snooze_expired, team_joined. Channels: in_app, email, push.

clear_pause.description: true to end a pause now.

include_ai_handled.description: Whether you are told about conversations the AI agent is answering.

paused_until.description: An RFC 3339 time, at most 30 days ahead, to pause everything until.

quiet_hours_bypass.description: Trigger keys that still come through during quiet hours.

quiet_hours_days.description: Days as a sum: Monday 1, Tuesday 2, Wednesday 4 and so on to Sunday 64; 127 is every day.

quiet_hours_enabled.description: Whether the caller's own quiet hours are on. The hours themselves are set with quiet_hours_start, quiet_hours_end and quiet_hours_days. Example: true.

quiet_hours_start.description: HH:MM on your clock. A window past midnight belongs to the day it starts.

show_previews.description: Whether email and push show the message text.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone for quiet hours. Empty follows your account's.

ids.description: Notification ids to mark, 100 at most. Leave out to mark all unread ones.

read.description: true for read, false for unread.

seen.description: true to clear the bell's badge without reading anything.

completed.description: true to finish setup for good.

step.description: The step reached: workspace, logo, channels, tags, team, knowledge, test_conversations or done.

cadence.description: How often the routine runs: "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "cron" or "once". "once" also needs run_at; the exact time otherwise comes from cron_expression. A routine runs at most once an hour. Such as "weekly".

cron_expression.description: A five-field cron expression, such as 0 9 * * 1 for Mondays at nine.

description.description: The description of the routine.

inbox_ids.description: Ids of inboxs, as a list, such as ["inbox_01jx2m8k4t"]. Find them with GET /inboxes.

name.description: The name of the routine.

notify_policy.description: When the routine tells people about a run: "on_findings" (only when it has suggestions), "always" (after every run that was not skipped) or "on_error_only" (only when a run fails). A pause is always told. Such as "on_findings".

owner_id.description: Id of the teammate (workspace member), starting with mem_, such as mem_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /members.

prompt.description: What to do, in plain words, such as Check the help articles for facts that went stale.

reset_state.description: Send true to forget what the routine kept between its runs, so the next run starts fresh. Left out or false, the kept state stays. Such as true.

run_at.description: The date and time a one-off routine runs, used only when cadence is "once". An ISO 8601 time still to come, such as "2026-12-01T09:00:00Z".

status.description: Pauses or resumes the routine: "paused" or "active". Resuming forgets past failures and works out the next run from now; a one-off routine with no run left also needs a new run_at. Such as "paused".

timezone.description: An IANA time zone, such as Europe/Lisbon.

brief_on_open.description: true has Operator brief a teammate when they open a conversation.

enabled.description: true to turn it on, false to turn it off.

instructions.description: How the team wants Operator to work, up to 8000 characters.

Returns the page to open, the attempt's state id and expiry, and for a device sign-in the code to type and how often to poll.
