parameters.description: A member id, mem_..., to read their log; needs members:write. Yours by default.
parameters.name: filter[member]

parameters.description: in_app, email, push or slack.
parameters.name: filter[channel]

parameters.description: sent, failed or skipped.
parameters.name: filter[status]

parameters.description: Leave out for the first page. To read the next page, pass the next_cursor the previous page returned.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: How many to return, up to 100. 25 by default.
parameters.name: limit

get.description: Lists the Slack channels the team hears in, and the person's own Slack direct message. Returns every destination with its type, what it hears about, its digests and status.

post.description: Makes a Slack channel of the workspace hear about the team's work, or links the person's own Slack direct message. A workspace posts to at most 25 channels. Returns the destination.

delete.description: Stops posting to a destination. Nothing changes in Slack itself. Returns nothing once it is removed.

parameters.description: Id of the notification destination, starting with ndst_, such as ndst_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /notification-destinations.
parameters.name: destination

get.description: Reads one destination: where it posts, what it hears about and when its next digest is due. Returns the destination.

parameters.description: Id of the notification destination, starting with ndst_, such as ndst_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /notification-destinations.
parameters.name: destination

patch.description: Changes what a destination hears about, its digests, or turns it off, or back on after an error. Fields left out stay as they are. Returns the destination as it now is.

parameters.description: Id of the notification destination, starting with ndst_, such as ndst_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /notification-destinations.
parameters.name: destination

post.description: Posts a test card to the destination now, to check the bot can reach it. Returns whether the post went through, with the error when it did not.

parameters.description: Id of the notification destination, starting with ndst_, such as ndst_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /notification-destinations.
parameters.name: destination

post.description: The dashboard's heartbeat: says whether the signed-in person's dashboard is visible and which conversation it shows, so dimmi knows what they are already looking at when it notifies them. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token.

delete.description: Puts every trigger and channel of your own settings back to the defaults. Returns your full notification settings as they now are.

get.description: Reads which things you are told about on which channel (in the app, email, push), with the defaults and locked cells, and your quiet hours and pause. Returns the triggers, channels, cells and settings.

patch.description: Turns triggers on or off per channel for yourself only. A cell set back to its default follows the default again. Returns your full notification settings as they now are.
Changes your own quiet hours, pause, previews and whether you hear about conversations the AI agent is answering. Only the fields sent change. Returns your settings as they now are.

post.description: Sends you, and only you, a test notification on one channel to check that it reaches you. Returns nothing.

delete.description: Turns the kind of notification email an unsubscribe link names back on, undoing an unsubscribe. Nobody signs in; the link's token is the proof. Returns the link's email, subscribed again.

parameters.description: The signed token from the unsubscribe link in the email. It names only its own member and kind of email.
parameters.name: token

get.description: Reads what an unsubscribe link in a teammate notification email names: the workspace, the address, the kind of email and whether it is still on. Nobody signs in; the link's token is the proof. Returns the workspace, email address, kind of email and whether it is subscribed.

parameters.description: The signed token from the unsubscribe link in the email. It names only its own member and kind of email.
parameters.name: token

patch.description: Turns off the kind of notification email an unsubscribe link names, for the member the link belongs to. Nobody signs in; the link's token is the proof. Returns the link's email, now unsubscribed.

parameters.description: The signed token from the unsubscribe link in the email. It names only its own member and kind of email.
parameters.name: token

get.description: Lists your own notifications, the bell in the app: new conversations, assignments, replies, mentions and approvals waiting, most recent first. Never anyone else's. Returns a page of notifications with unread_count, unseen_count and next_cursor in meta.

parameters.description: unread for unread ones only; all (default) for every one.
parameters.name: filter[status]

parameters.description: One trigger key, such as mentioned or conversation_assigned.
parameters.name: filter[trigger]

parameters.description: Leave out for the first page. To read the next page, pass the next_cursor the previous page returned.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: How many to return, up to 100. 20 by default.
parameters.name: limit

patch.description: Marks your own notifications read or unread, or the bell seen. With no ids, read marks every unread one. Returns the bell's unread_count and unseen_count after the change.

get.description: Lists each channel one of your own notifications went to, and how it ended. Returns the deliveries of the notification, oldest first.

parameters.description: Id of the notification, starting with ntf_, such as ntf_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /notifications.
parameters.name: notification

get.summary: Show how a notification reached you

get.description: Reads an app's request to act for the signed-in person, for the consent screen: which app, where it sends the answer, the access it asks for and the workspaces the person may connect it to. The request is checked on every call. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns the app's request with the access asked for and the workspaces on offer.

parameters.description: The whole query string the app sent to the authorization page, up to 8000 characters, such as client_id=abc&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code. Required.
parameters.name: query

post.description: Records the signed-in person's decision on an app's request to act for them. An approval names one of their active workspaces and the access to give, never more than the app asked for; the person's role still limits what the app can do. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns the address to send the person to: back to the app with a code, or with the news that they refused.

get.description: Lists the changes Operator proposed that you may review, newest first: pending, applied, declined, reverted or failed. Returns the changesets with their title, reason, status and the operations each holds.

parameters.description: Only changes about this conversation (conv_...).
parameters.name: filter[conversation]

parameters.description: Only changes this routine suggested (ort_...).
parameters.name: filter[routine]

parameters.description: Only changes in this state.
parameters.name: filter[status]

post.description: Applies every operation of a changeset as you, in one go: it changes real data, such as tags, assignments, statuses, notes, contacts, article drafts, and can run AI actions in the workspace's systems. Show the operations and apply only when the person agrees. Returns the changeset as applied, or failed with why and nothing changed.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator changeset, starting with opc_, such as opc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/changesets.
parameters.name: changeset

post.description: Turns down a changeset Operator proposed. Nothing changes. Returns the changeset, declined.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator changeset, starting with opc_, such as opc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/changesets.
parameters.name: changeset

post.description: Undoes an applied changeset, newest operation first. A field someone changed since is left as they set it. Returns the changeset, reverted.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator changeset, starting with opc_, such as opc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/changesets.
parameters.name: changeset

get.description: Searches the knowledge the AI agent answers customers from: published help articles and connected sources. Use it to find what the help center already says about something. Returns up to 8 passages, each with its title, article_id when it is from an article, url and text.

parameters.description: What to look for, in a few words, such as refund window.
parameters.name: search_text

get.description: Lists what you asked Operator to remember. Memories are yours alone. Returns your memories, newest first.

delete.description: Makes Operator forget one of your memories.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator memory, starting with opy_, such as opy_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/memories.
parameters.name: memory

get.description: Lists the templates a routine can start from, with their prompt, cadence and what they need. Returns the templates, the custom one last.
Lists the workspace's routines: prompts Operator runs on a clock and reports on. Returns the routines with their cadence, next run, status and last outcome.

parameters.description: active, paused or completed.
parameters.name: filter[status]

post.description: Puts Operator on a clock: a prompt it runs daily, weekly, monthly, on a cron or once, leaving suggestions the team reviews. Every run spends the workspace's AI budget. Confirm the prompt and cadence with the person first. Returns the routine with its next runs.

delete.description: Stops a routine for good. Its threads and suggestions stay.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator routine, starting with ort_, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/routines.
parameters.name: routine

get.description: Reads one routine: its prompt, when it runs, what it may read and change, and this month's spend. Returns the routine with its next three runs and its spend this month in micro-dollars.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator routine, starting with ort_, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/routines.
parameters.name: routine

patch.description: Changes a routine's prompt, cadence, access or delivery, pauses or resumes it, or makes it forget what it kept between runs. Returns the routine as changed.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator routine, starting with ort_, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/routines.
parameters.name: routine

post.description: Says a run of a routine found nothing that needs the team's attention, so nobody is notified. Call it at the end of a run that suggested nothing. Returns recorded (false for a dry run) and a message.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator routine, starting with ort_, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/routines.
parameters.name: routine

get.description: Lists a routine's runs, newest first. Returns the runs with their trigger, outcome, suggestions, cost and thread.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator routine, starting with ort_, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/routines.
parameters.name: routine

post.description: Runs a routine now. A dry run reads real data but leaves only previews and keeps no state; a live run leaves real suggestions. Both spend the AI budget. Returns the queued run; read it again to see how it went.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator routine, starting with ort_, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/routines.
parameters.name: routine

get.description: Reads one run of a routine: how it went, why it was skipped or failed, and its thread. Returns the run.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator routine, starting with ort_, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/routines.
parameters.name: routine

parameters.description: Id of the run, starting with wfr or air_, such as wfr_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with the matching runs list.
parameters.name: run

get.description: Reads what a routine kept from its earlier runs, such as cursors and what it covered. Returns the state as a JSON object, empty when nothing was saved.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator routine, starting with ort_, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/routines.
parameters.name: routine

patch.description: Saves what the next run of a routine needs, as a JSON object of at most 64 KB. Keys given replace the saved ones; every other saved key stays. Returns the state as it now stands, and saved (false for a dry run).

parameters.description: Id of the Operator routine, starting with ort_, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/routines.
parameters.name: routine

get.description: Reads how Operator is set up for the workspace: on or off, briefs, triage, instructions and policies. Returns the settings with each group's policy and the groups that may apply at once.

patch.description: Changes Operator for the whole workspace, including which changes it may apply without asking. Only the fields sent change; policies merge by group. Returns the settings as they now are.

get.description: Lists the skills: the steps for doing each kind of routine work well, and when to read each. Returns the skills with skill_name and when_to_use.
Reads how to do one kind of routine work well, step by step, before starting it. Returns the skill with its steps.

parameters.description: The skill's name, such as audit_articles. Find the names with GET /operator/skills.
parameters.name: skill

post.description: Suggests a fix to one help article: the passages to replace, each quoted from the article with what it should say instead. A teammate reviews it; the article changes only when they approve. Read the article with GET /articles/{article} first. Call it once per article. Returns made (false when the same suggestion was made before), a message saying what happened, and the suggestion a teammate reviews.
post.summary: Suggest a fix to an article

post.description: Suggests changes to conversations and customers as one suggestion a teammate reviews: tag or untag, assign, set priority, open or close, rename, add an internal note, update a customer's name, or add a regression test to a procedure. Articles and procedure edits have their own tools: POST /operator/suggestions/article-edits, POST /operator/suggestions/new-articles and POST /operator/suggestions/procedure-edits. Returns made (false when the same suggestion was made before), a message saying what happened, and the suggestion a teammate reviews.

Suggests a new help article as a draft a teammate reviews; nothing is created until they approve. Call it once per article. Returns made (false when the same suggestion was made before), a message saying what happened, and the suggestion a teammate reviews.

Suggests an edit to one procedure's working copy. A teammate reviews it; the procedure changes only when they approve. Read it with GET /procedures/{procedure} first. Call it once per procedure. Returns made (false when the same suggestion was made before), a message saying what happened, and the suggestion a teammate reviews.
post.summary: Suggest an edit to a procedure

get.description: Lists the changes suggested lately, newest first, each with its status, dedup_key and what it changes in a line. Call it before suggesting, so nothing is suggested twice. Returns up to 50 suggestions with status, suggested_on, suggestion_title, dedup_key and changes.

parameters.description: How many days back to look, from 1 to 90, such as 30. 30 when left out.
parameters.name: days_back

parameters.description: Only suggestions with this status, such as pending. Leave out for all.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Only suggestions made for this routine, such as ort_01jx2m8k4t. Leave out for all.
parameters.name: routine_id

get.description: Lists your own threads with Operator, the team's agent, latest first. Threads are private. Returns the threads with their title, conversation and last message time.

parameters.description: Only threads about the whole workspace.
parameters.name: filter[scope]

parameters.description: Only threads about this conversation (conv_...).
parameters.name: filter[conversation]

parameters.description: The shared threads of this routine's runs (ort_...).
parameters.name: filter[routine]

post.description: Opens your latest thread with Operator about a conversation, or starts one; without a conversation it starts a thread about the whole workspace. Opening spends nothing. Returns the thread with its messages, oldest first, and the changes Operator proposed in it.

delete.description: Deletes one of your own threads with Operator and its messages. Changes already applied stay.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator thread, starting with opt_, such as opt_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/threads.
parameters.name: thread

get.description: Reads one of your threads with Operator. Returns the thread with its messages, oldest first, and the changesets proposed in it.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator thread, starting with opt_, such as opt_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/threads.
parameters.name: thread

post.description: Asks Operator a question or gives it a task on a thread and waits for its answer. Every question runs real models and spends the workspace's AI budget. Operator proposes changes as changesets to apply; groups set to auto in its settings apply at once. Returns your message, Operator's answer and the changesets it proposed.

parameters.description: Id of the Operator thread, starting with opt_, such as opt_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /operator/threads.
parameters.name: thread

get.description: Reads one month of Operator's runs: cost, tokens, failures, by purpose, teammate and model, and what became of its changesets. Months are counted in UTC; the spending cap is shared with the AI agent. Returns the month's cost in micro-dollars, counts, daily series, breakdowns and latest runs.

parameters.description: The month as YYYY-MM. Leave out for the current month.
parameters.name: period

get.description: Lists the email domains the organization behind the current workspace added, each with its status, the record that proves it and the connection its sign-ins go to. It needs the permission to manage single sign-on, which owners hold. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns every domain of the organization.

post.description: Adds an email domain the company wants to prove it owns, and answers with the record to publish as proof; an organization has at most twenty. Public suffixes and free mail domains are refused, and a domain already added is returned as it is. It needs the permission to manage single sign-on, which owners hold. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code. Returns the domain, pending, with the name and value of the record that proves it.

delete.description: Removes a domain from the organization; one routed to an enforced connection is refused. It needs the permission to manage single sign-on, which owners hold. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code.

parameters.description: The domain's id from the list of organization domains, such as odom_4f9k2.
parameters.name: domain

patch.description: Sends the sign-ins of a verified domain to a single sign-on connection, or to none. A domain routed to an enforced connection cannot be moved away. It needs the permission to manage single sign-on, which owners hold. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code. Returns the domain as it now is.

parameters.description: The domain's id from the list of organization domains, such as odom_4f9k2.
parameters.name: domain

patch.summary: Route a domain to a connection

post.description: Looks up the proof record of a domain now. A record found makes the domain verified, unless another organization already holds it; none found leaves it pending. It needs the permission to manage single sign-on, which owners hold. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns the check's status, the records found and the domain.

parameters.description: The domain's id from the list of organization domains, such as odom_4f9k2.
parameters.name: domain

post.description: Mails a link that sets a new password; it works for 60 minutes and replaces any earlier one. It answers the same for every address, so it never tells whether an account exists. Anyone may call it before signing in. Returns a message saying the link was sent if the address has an account.

patch.description: Redeems a mailed reset link: sets the new password, ends every session, app connection and access token of the account, and signs the person in on this browser. Only a browser or app holding the link can call it. Returns the signed-in person, or the second-factor challenge to answer.

parameters.description: The id from the reset link, such as prs_4f9k2. It proves nothing without the token.
parameters.name: reset

get.description: Lists every permission a role is made of, with its name and what it allows, in the reader's language, and whether a custom role may hold it. Returns the permissions with key, group, label, description, assignable and the base roles it fits.
Lists the procedures, the step-by-step playbooks the AI agent follows for kinds of requests. Returns every procedure with its status and how many conversations used it in 30 days.

post.description: Creates an empty draft procedure. The agent does not follow it until published. Returns the draft procedure.

delete.description: Deletes a procedure. The agent stops following it at once if it was live.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

get.description: Reads one procedure's working copy and whether it differs from the live one. Returns the procedure with its definition, status and lock_version.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

patch.description: Saves the name or the working copy of a procedure. Customers see no change until it is published. Returns the procedure as saved, with its new lock_version.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

get.description: Reads how a procedure did in real conversations: how often it ran, finished and handed over. Returns the counts, rates, a daily series and where conversations left the procedure.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

parameters.description: How many days back, up to 90.
parameters.name: days

parameters.description: Only conversations on this published version.
parameters.name: version

delete.description: Takes a procedure out of the AI agent's hands at once. The working copy stays. Returns the procedure, unpublished.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

post.description: Makes the working copy live: the AI agent follows it with customers from the next message. Every action it takes must exist and be published. Returns the procedure, published.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

post.description: Sends one customer message to the AI agent as it would follow this procedure, and returns its reply. Nothing reaches a customer and actions answer with their saved test result, never your systems. Every turn runs real models and spends the workspace's AI budget. Returns the agent's reply, the actions it called, the procedure's state to send with the next turn.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

get.description: Lists the saved simulations of a procedure and how each last went. Returns the simulations with their messages, checks and last result.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

post.description: Saves a chat as a simulation: an AI-played customer replays it against the procedure, on the date it was saved, and the checks say whether the agent did what it should. Returns the saved simulation.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

post.description: Runs a procedure's saved simulations against its working copy and waits for the verdicts. Each run calls real models for the agent, the customer and the checks, and spends the workspace's AI budget. A working copy with problems to fix is not run. Returns each simulation with its result: passed, failed or an error, and every check's verdict.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

delete.description: Deletes a saved simulation and its last result.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

parameters.description: Id of the procedure simulation, starting with prct_, such as prct_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures/{procedure}/test-cases.
parameters.name: test_case

get.description: Reads one saved simulation of a procedure and its last result. Returns the simulation with its messages, checks, date and last result turn by turn.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

parameters.description: Id of the procedure simulation, starting with prct_, such as prct_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures/{procedure}/test-cases.
parameters.name: test_case

patch.description: Changes a saved simulation's name, messages, customer or checks. Returns the simulation as saved.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

parameters.description: Id of the procedure simulation, starting with prct_, such as prct_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures/{procedure}/test-cases.
parameters.name: test_case

get.description: Lists every published version of a procedure, newest first, with who published it and why. Returns the versions with their number, note and publish time.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

parameters.description: Version number to page from.
parameters.name: before

parameters.description: At most 100.
parameters.name: limit

get.description: Reads one published version of a procedure as it was. Returns the version with its full definition.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

parameters.description: Id of the saved version, starting with prcv or srsv_, such as prcv_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with the matching versions list.
parameters.name: version

post.description: Copies a published version into the working copy. Customers see no change until it is published again. Returns the procedure with the restored working copy.

parameters.description: Id of the AI agent procedure, starting with prc_, such as prc_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /procedures.
parameters.name: procedure

parameters.description: Id of the saved version, starting with prcv or srsv_, such as prcv_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with the matching versions list.
parameters.name: version

get.description: Reads the public key a browser needs to subscribe to push notifications from this dimmi server. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns the server's VAPID public key and its key id.

Lists the browsers the signed-in person turned push notifications on in. They belong to the person across workspaces, and their keys are never shown. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns the person's push devices.

post.description: Registers the browser's push subscription so the signed-in person gets push notifications on it. The values come from the browser's own push subscription, so only that browser can call it. Returns the registered device.

delete.description: Removes one of the signed-in person's push devices, so it stops getting push notifications. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token.

parameters.description: The device's id from the list of push devices, such as psub_4f9k2.
parameters.name: subscription

get.description: Reads what is masked out of messages before they are stored: the built-in rules for card numbers and US social security numbers, then the workspace's own patterns in the order they run. Returns the built-in switches and the workspace's rules in order.

patch.description: Turns the built-in redaction rules on or off and puts the workspace's own rules in a new order. Applies to messages stored from now on; earlier messages are never rewritten. Returns the built-in switches and the rules in their new order.

post.description: Adds a pattern whose matches are replaced in every message stored from now on, with no copy of the original kept. It runs after the others. A workspace keeps at most 10 rules. Returns the rule as saved.

delete.description: Removes a rule from the next message on. What it already replaced stays replaced. Returns nothing once it is removed.

parameters.description: Id of the redaction rule, starting with rxr_, such as rxr_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /redaction-rules.
parameters.name: redaction_rule

patch.description: Changes a rule's name, pattern or replacement, or switches it off. Messages it already changed stay as they were stored. Returns the rule as it now is.

parameters.description: Id of the redaction rule, starting with rxr_, such as rxr_01jx2m8k4t. Find it with GET /redaction-rules.
parameters.name: redaction_rule

post.description: Shows what the workspace's enabled redaction rules would make of a text, and which rules matched. Nothing is stored and the text is never logged. Returns the text as it would be stored and the rules that changed it.

delete.description: Stops mailing the reports to the caller. Returns nothing.

get.description: Reads whether the caller gets the reports by mail, how often, and what the digest covers. Returns the frequency, null when there is none, the filters and when it next goes.

patch.description: Has the overview mailed to the caller each morning or each Monday, compared with the period before. Returns the digest as saved, with when it next goes.

get.description: Lists the reports the caller may read: overview, responsiveness, resolution, team, live workload, satisfaction, AI, help center and any others the workspace has. Returns each report's key, title and one line about it, and whether it shows the present instead of a range.
Compares every procedure's runs, completions and handovers over a period. Returns one row per procedure with its counts and rates.

parameters.description: First day, YYYY-MM-DD.
parameters.name: from

OpenID Connect needs an issuer, a client id and a client secret; SAML settings can be sent now or later. It still has to be tested and made active. It needs the permission to manage single sign-on, which owners hold. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code. Returns the new connection in draft.

delete.description: Deletes a single sign-on connection of the organization; one that is enforced is refused until enforcement is turned off. It needs the permission to manage single sign-on, which owners hold. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code.

Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code. Returns the connection as it now is.

Returns the new token with its secret, shown only once.

get.description: Reads the account of the person this connection acts for: name, email, language and time zone. Returns the person's account.

patch.description: Changes the signed-in person's own name, language, time zone or personal preferences; a field left out stays as it is. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns the person's account as it now is.

delete.description: Removes every second factor of the signed-in person, which turns two-factor authentication off; when it was not on, only unfinished factors are deleted. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code.

get.description: Lists the signed-in person's own second factors: authenticator apps, passkeys and recovery codes, pending or active, and which one is preferred. post.description: Starts adding a second factor to the signed-in person's account, or makes a fresh set of recovery codes. The factor stays pending until the factor update activates it with its first code or signed passkey. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code. Returns the pending factor with its setup (secret and QR code, or passkey options), or the new recovery codes.

delete.description: Removes one of the signed-in person's own factors. Removing the last one that keeps two-factor authentication on turns it off; recovery codes cannot be removed while it is on. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code.

parameters.description: The factor's id from the list of second factors, such as fac_4f9k2.

Activating is a step of its own; five wrong answers delete the pending factor. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns the factor as it now is, with new recovery codes when it turned two-factor authentication on.

parameters.description: The factor's id from the list of second factors, such as fac_4f9k2.

Mails the signed-in person a six-digit code to confirm who they are, good for ten minutes. It is only for an account without a password, at most one a minute and five an hour; an account with a password is refused. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns a message saying the code was sent.

delete.description: Moves the current workspace to the trash, revokes its access tokens and withdraws its pending invitations; it is purged for good when the grace period ends unless an owner restores it. Only an owner's own browser or app can call it, after confirming who they are recently. Returns the workspace as it sits in the trash.

get.description: Reads the workspace this connection works in: its name, address, time zone and main settings. Every tool acts inside this one workspace. Returns the workspace.

patch.description: Changes the workspace's name, address (slug), language, time zone, the name customers see, composer options, link checks and how long data is kept. Only the fields sent change. A new slug keeps the old address pointing here for thirty days. Returns the workspace as it now is.

get.description: Reads how people may sign in to the workspace: allowed sign-in methods and Google domains, session limits, IP allowlists for the dashboard and the API, two-factor and single sign-on. Returns the rules, the caller's own IP and how many tokens are used from outside the API allowlist.

patch.description: Changes the workspace's access rules: allowed ways of signing in, Google domains, session limits and IP allowlists. A key left out stays as it is and a list replaces the whole stored list. It needs the permission to manage the security policy, and a change that would lock the caller out is refused. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, right after confirming their password or mailed code. Returns the access rules as they now are.

get.description: Reads how many API requests a minute this workspace may make; zero means no limit. Returns the workspace's request limits.

delete.description: Takes the workspace logo down, so customers see the workspace without one. Removing it twice is fine. Returns nothing.

put.description: Replaces the workspace's logo with an uploaded image. It needs a file sent as a multipart form in the field named logo, and the settings:write permission. Returns the workspace with its new logo.

filename.description: filename of the file being uploaded

name.description: general purpose name for multipart form value

patch.description: Records how far a new workspace's setup has come, so it resumes on any device. Completing it opens the app for everyone and is final: the workspace never goes back to setup. Returns the workspace with its onboarding state.

post.description: Starts five made-up conversations from pretend customers, so the team can practice replying, tagging and closing. They are marked as tests: never billed and never sent anywhere. Returns how many practice conversations started.
Creates a new workspace, with its own organization, owned by the signed-in person. Only a signed-in person's browser or app can call it, never an API token. Returns the new workspace.

patch.description: Brings a deleted workspace back from the trash; the only change it takes is trashed false. Only an active owner's own browser or app can call it, after confirming who they are recently, and only until the grace period ends. Every other setting changes through the workspace update instead. Returns the workspace as it now is.

parameters.description: The id of the workspace to restore, such as ws_4f9k2.
parameters.name: workspace
